title: Rosetta Decipherment and Collaborative Evidence
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
The Rosetta Stone bears versions of a decree in hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Greek writing. The three inscriptions are not mechanically identical line by line, yet their overlapping content created a rare comparative resource. Scholars could begin with the readable Greek and test correspondences in the Egyptian texts. Comparison did not supply an automatic dictionary; it narrowed the range of defensible guesses.

Proper names offered especially useful anchors. Oval frames now called cartouches appeared to enclose royal names. Thomas Young connected signs in such frames with sounds in names including Ptolemy and identified several phonetic values. His work was a major advance, but he did not fully generalize phonetic writing across the Egyptian system. A correct local inference can therefore coexist with an incomplete general model.

Jean-François Champollion combined comparative inscriptions with deep knowledge of Coptic, a later stage of the Egyptian language. He recognized that hieroglyphic writing could use signs in several ways, including phonetic and semantic functions. His 1822 announcement marked a decisive expansion of the decipherment. Yet “decisive” should not erase the work of Young, earlier scholars, copyists, collectors, and the Egyptian linguistic continuity preserved in Coptic.

Decipherment is best understood as iterative model testing. A proposed sound value must work beyond one famous name; a reading should explain additional inscriptions without ad hoc exceptions. Historical credit matters, but the deeper lesson is methodological: evidence becomes powerful when independent constraints converge. The stone did not speak by itself. People learned to ask it questions that could fail.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Greek supplied a complete automatic translation of every sign.

options.label: B
options.text: Decipherment emerged through constrained comparison, partial advances, and broader testing.

options.label: C
options.text: Young made no useful contribution.

options.label: D
options.text: Hieroglyphs function exactly like a modern alphabet.

questions.answer: 正解：B。重なる碑文、固有名、Youngの局所的音価、Coptic、Champollionの一般化、別碑文での検証が収束しました。Aは比較を自動翻訳化し、C・Dは貢献と複数機能を消します。

questions.prompt: Why were three scripts valuable without providing an automatic translation?

options.label: A
options.text: Readable Greek and overlapping content narrowed possible correspondences, but the versions were not line-by-line identical and sign functions still required testing elsewhere.

options.label: B
options.text: Every line and sign was mechanically identical across all three inscriptions.

options.label: C
options.text: Greek directly listed a complete dictionary for every Egyptian sign.

options.label: D
options.text: The Egyptian texts could be ignored once the Greek decree was read.

questions.answer: 正解：A。読めるギリシャ語は対応候補を絞りましたが、三版は逐語一致せず、記号が音・語・意味のどれを担うか別資料で検証する必要がありました。B～Dは比較の限界を消します。

questions.prompt: The word “anchors” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: clues that stabilize a comparison

options.label: B
options.text: tools used to move the stone

options.label: C
options.text: exceptions that defeat a theory

options.label: D
options.text: decorative ovals with no linguistic role

questions.answer: 正解：A。既知の王名は未知の記号との対応を固定する手がかりでした。物理的な錨ではなく、比較推論を安定させる既知要素の比喩です。

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly identifies both Young's contribution and its limitation?

options.label: A
options.text: He identified several phonetic values from royal names but did not fully generalize phonetic writing across the Egyptian system.

options.label: B
options.text: He produced a complete dictionary but found no phonetic values.

options.label: C
options.text: He proved that every hieroglyph had only a semantic function.

options.label: D
options.text: He rejected cartouches as irrelevant decorations.

questions.answer: 正解：A。Youngはカルトゥーシュ内の王名から複数の音価を同定しましたが、表音性を文字体系全体へ十分一般化しませんでした。局所的に正しい推論と不完全な一般モデルは両立します。

questions.prompt: Why did knowledge of Coptic help Champollion decipher hieroglyphs?

options.label: A
options.text: Coptic, a later stage of the Egyptian language, supplied linguistic sounds and words against which readings from the older script could be tested.

options.label: B
options.text: Coptic and hieroglyphs were identical scripts written in the same period.

options.label: C
options.text: Coptic proved that hieroglyphic signs could have no phonetic function.

options.label: D
options.text: Knowledge of language was unnecessary once the stone was found.

questions.answer: 正解：A。hieroglyphicは書記体系、Copticはエジプト語の後代段階です。後者の語彙・音の知識で、前者の記号から復元した音列を実在言語として検査できました。B～Dはscriptとlanguageを混同します。

questions.prompt: Which statement is best supported by the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: A breakthrough must be independent of all prior work.

options.label: B
options.text: One correct reading proves a model for the whole writing system.

options.label: C
options.text: A reading gains strength when it works across additional inscriptions.

options.label: D
options.text: Historical credit is irrelevant to understanding scholarship.

questions.answer: 正解：C。提案した音価や読みが一つの有名な名前だけでなく別碑文も説明すれば、一般モデルの証拠が強まります。Aは先行研究を、Bは反復検証を、Dは功績配分を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why is it inaccurate to say that the stone itself decoded ancient Egyptian?

options.label: A
options.text: The stone supplied comparative evidence, but researchers proposed correspondences and tested them with other inscriptions and linguistic knowledge.

options.label: B
options.text: The stone contained no inscriptions or overlapping content.

options.label: C
options.text: Only the stone, not people, could formulate and reject hypotheses.

options.label: D
options.text: Finding evidence and interpreting it are always the same action.

questions.answer: 正解：A。石は比較可能な証拠を提供しましたが、対応仮説を立て、別碑文とCopticで検証したのは研究者です。資料の存在と解読行為を同一視してはいけません。B～Dはその区別を逆転します。

questions.prompt: What does “People learned to ask it questions that could fail” imply about scientific method?

options.label: A
options.text: Useful hypotheses make predictions that evidence can contradict, allowing competing readings to be rejected.

options.label: B
options.text: A good explanation must be protected from every possible test.

options.label: C
options.text: Researchers should add ad hoc exceptions whenever a reading fails.

options.label: D
options.text: Any story is acceptable if it concerns an ancient object.

questions.answer: 正解：A。「人々は、その石に対して、失敗し得る問いを投げかける方法を学んだ」。予測が外れる可能性を持つ仮説だから、証拠によって読みを選別できます。B～Dは反証可能性を避けます。

questions.prompt: Which revision best corrects the claim that Champollion alone decoded hieroglyphs in one sudden moment?

options.label: A
options.text: Champollion decisively integrated and extended multilingual comparison, Young's phonetic values, Coptic continuity, and tests on other inscriptions into a more general account.

options.label: B
options.text: Champollion's achievement was unrelated to earlier scholarship, Coptic, or comparative inscriptions.

options.label: C
options.text: Young completed the whole decipherment, so Champollion contributed nothing.

options.label: D
options.text: The stone automatically revealed every reading without iterative testing.

questions.answer: 正解：A。Champollionの1822年の飛躍を認めつつ、多言語碑文、Youngの音価、Coptic、別碑文での検証という連鎖に位置づけます。先行貢献の明示は彼の重要性を弱めず、B～Dは単独英雄か逆の抹消です。
